# Updating a feature branch by rebase instead of merge. During a rebase git makes
# the upstream "ours", so develop's entries stay first and develop's log stays a
# plain prefix - also when develop moves on again.

sesam-repo admin base.txt dev.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'
exec git branch develop

# feature: own entry F.
exec git checkout -b feature
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'feature: tell bob'

# develop: D1 meanwhile.
exec git checkout develop
cp $TMPDIR/dev.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'develop: reseal s'

# Update feature by rebase.
exec git checkout feature
exec git rebase develop
exec sesam verify --truncate
stderr 'Audit log history: ok'

# develop moves on (D3) before the feature lands; feature updates again.
exec git checkout develop
exec sesam tell --user carol --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'develop: tell carol'

exec git checkout feature
exec git rebase develop
exec sesam verify --truncate
stderr 'Audit log history: ok'

# Squash into develop, GitHub-style (no drivers, no hooks).
exec git checkout develop
exec git merge --squash feature
exec git commit --no-verify -m 'squash feature'
exec sesam verify --truncate
stderr 'Audit log history: ok'
exec sesam user ls
stdout bob
stdout carol

-- base.txt --
S=BASE
-- dev.txt --
S=DEV
